findings.title: Dynamic Multi-Pair Trading Strategy in Cryptocurrency Markets with Deep Reinforcement Learning
findings.summary: LSTM-PPO execution overlay for crypto pairs. 'Filter-then-Rank' pair selection + Fixed Risk Adaptive Mean execution model. OOS outperforms heuristic baseline (p<0.10 bootstrap). Hierarchical architecture separates pair selection from execution policy.
findings.reason: Pairs family exhausted on equity side (H200 NOT CONFIRMED). Crypto pairs angle partially covered by H264b (already staged). The LSTM-PPO execution overlay idea is interesting but requires crypto infrastructure. Not staging — overlaps with H264b.

findings.title: Copula-Based Trading of Cointegrated Cryptocurrency Pairs
findings.summary: Non-linear cointegration via copulas. Cryptocurrency market focus.
findings.reason: Older paper (2023). Pairs family exhausted on equity side. Not staging.

scan_angles.angle: arXiv: PEAD + post-earnings drift + text signals + NLP

findings.title: ChatGPT in Systematic Investing — Enhancing Risk-Adjusted Returns with LLMs
findings.summary: LLM conditions cross-sectional momentum entries on news confirmation. S&P 500 constituents. Higher Sharpe/Sortino IS and truly OOS. Robust to costs (up to 30bps/leg). Strongest for concentrated portfolios. October 2025.
findings.reason: Directly upgrades H228 (alpha101+reversal, OOS 1.572) and H198 (momentum, OOS 1.174). LLM as news-confirmation filter before entering momentum positions. STAGED as H279.

findings.title: Signal or Noise in Multi-Agent LLM-based Stock Recommendations?
findings.summary: MarketSenseAI live validation. 4 specialist agents + synthesis. Strong-buy portfolio +2.18%/month vs +1.15% benchmark (19 months, p=0.003). ICIR=+0.489 (p=0.024). Agent contributions rotate by regime.
findings.reason: Strongest live OOS validation of multi-agent LLM equity signal seen to date. No look-ahead bias (live generation). STAGED as H280.

findings.title: Autonomous Market Intelligence: Agentic AI Nowcasting Predicts Stock Returns
findings.summary: Fully agentic LLM (web search, no curated text) evaluating Russell 1000 daily from April 2025. Top-20 ranked: 18.4bps/day alpha, Sharpe 2.43. Predictability asymmetric — only top tier works; bottom tier = noise.
findings.reason: Interesting but very short live track record (~14 months). Daily rebalancing on Russell 1000 has high transaction costs. The top-20 concentration partially overlaps with H280 approach. Not staging separately — overlap with H279/H280 covered.

findings.title: Not All Factors Crowd Equally: Modeling, Measuring, and Trading on Alpha Decay
findings.summary: Derives hyperbolic decay K/(1+λt) from game-theoretic model. Validated on 8 FF factors 1963-2024. Momentum: R²=0.65 hyperbolic >> linear/exponential. Crowding post-2015 accelerated. KEY FINDING: crowding predicts crash RISK not mean return — crowded reversal 1.7-1.8x crash prob, crowded momentum 0.38x (safer!).
findings.reason: Updates signal-halflife.md with: (1) game-theory foundation for hyperbolic form, (2) crash-risk finding (crowding ≠ lower returns, = higher tail risk for reversal), (3) Python fitting code. STAGED as wiki update.

findings.title: Continuous Timing Signals for Growth-Defensive Style Allocation
findings.summary: Smooth macro timing score (rate relief + SPY drawdown + VIX stress + growth-crowding penalty) for growth vs defensive ETF tilt. CAGR 19.24%, Sharpe 1.01, MaxDD -31.63% (2017-2026). Improves over 50/50 but doesn't beat pure growth in CAGR.
findings.reason: Smooth macro timing score concept is related to H249/H165 regime work (already confirmed). The specific G/D allocation framework is less relevant — we already have H026 momentum-based rotation. Adds to regime-detection.md as supporting evidence for continuous score approach. Not staging new hypothesis.

findings.title: Macro Economists in the Machine: Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Commodity-Related ETF Portfolio Construction
findings.summary: Hawkish/Dovish/Debate agents all receive identical FRED macro z-scores. All 3 LLM agents beat Rule Agent in Sharpe (Hawkish ΔSharpe=+0.044, Debate ΔSharpe=+0.040, p<0.10). Debate = bias correction not new alpha. Net advantage up to 30bps one-way costs.
findings.reason: Directly applicable to H026 production ETF rotation — adding FRED macro z-score LLM interpretation as tilt modifier. STAGED as H281.

findings.title: Beyond Agent Architecture: Execution Assumptions and Reproducibility in LLM-Based Trading Systems
findings.summary: 30-study reproducibility audit of LLM trading research. Most papers weak on PIT controls, split transparency, cost modeling, execution semantics. '10-equity worked example' shows explicit friction/timing choices materially compress results.
findings.reason: Validates our shared eval checklist approach. Adds 'execution semantics' as specific evaluation dimension. Already cited in new execution-quality.md wiki page. Wiki update to shared-eval-checklist.md warranted but minor — execution semantics already partially covered. Not staging separately.

findings.title: TT-DAC-PS: Twin-Target Deterministic Actor-Critic with Policy Smoothing for Optimal Trade Execution
findings.summary: RL approach to optimal execution of large stock sell programs. TD3-style twin critic + EWMA target smoothing. Addresses Almgren-Chriss framework limitations.
findings.reason: Optimal execution is not our current bottleneck at $100k AUM. Relevant when scaling to $1M+. Note for future reference.

findings.title: virattt/ai-hedge-fund
findings.summary: Multi-agent LLM hedge fund simulation. Educational. 11 specialist agents (Warren Buffett, Bill Ackman, etc.) debate each stock. No production backtesting rigor — single entry/exit, no cost modeling.
findings.reason: High star count but limited production value. Educational reference for multi-agent design patterns. Already noted in CLAUDE.local.md. Not staging.

findings.title: AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRL
findings.summary: Deep RL for trading. Already noted in wiki (deep-rl-trading.md).
findings.reason: Already in wiki. H204 NOT CONFIRMED for RL approach. No new developments.

scan_angles.angle: arXiv: post-selection Sharpe estimation + backtesting methodology

findings.title: Post Selection Estimation of Sharpe Ratios
findings.summary: Estimates true Sharpe of strategy selected for highest IS Sharpe among many. James-Stein shrinkage best performer across simulations (bias, RMSE, rank correlation). Relevant when we select H-hypotheses based on OOS Sharpe.
findings.reason: Adds to multiple-testing.md: when we select the best hypothesis from a set, IS Sharpe is biased upward; James-Stein shrinkage provides better OOS estimate. Low-risk wiki update. Cited in execution-quality.md. Could be added to multiple-testing.md in a future session — not urgent.

session2_additional_searches.angle: arXiv: pairs trading + cointegration + LLM (deeper search)

findings.title: No new LLM + pairs trading papers found (2025-2026)
findings.reason: The LLM + pairs trading combination does not appear to have active 2025-2026 research. Most recent work (H200 NOT CONFIRMED on graphical matching) remains the frontier. Equity pairs family exhausted. Crypto pairs covered by H264b.

findings.title: Predicting Stock Price Direction on Earnings Announcement Days using Multi-modal Deep Learning
findings.summary: Combines 15 fundamental metrics + 3 price technicals + FinBERT sentiment. Transformer > LSTM. Ablation confirms FinBERT adds value. No trading metrics provided (Sharpe/WR not reported).
findings.reason: Validates multi-modal signal fusion for earnings. But no trading performance metrics, only classification (direction accuracy not reported). Too thin for hypothesis staging without performance data. Supports adding price technicals to existing H163/H174 pipeline as future H284 — but need a paper with actual trading results first.

findings.title: Extracting the Structure of Press Releases for Predicting Earnings Announcement Returns
findings.summary: FinBERT highest predictive power across 138K press releases 2005-2023. Press release soft info = EPS surprise in informativeness. Key caveat: 'stock prices fully reflect press release content at market open' — implies PEAD must be traded pre-open.
findings.reason: Validates our H163/H174 approach (FinBERT on 8-K). The 'prices reflect at open' finding CONFIRMS why our pipeline uses OPG (opening gap) entries — we need to be in before market open to capture the drift. Not staging new hypothesis; confirms existing architecture.

findings.title: Cross-sectional factor momentum: evidence from multiple formation periods
findings.summary: Recent and intermediate-past formation periods produce significant factor momentum. Published Applied Economics Letters 2025.
findings.reason: Confirms existing factor momentum findings but doesn't add new actionable angle beyond what H255/H256 tested. Not staging.

findings.title: QuantaAlpha: An Evolutionary Framework for LLM-Driven Alpha Mining
findings.summary: GPT-5.2 + evolutionary algorithm for factor discovery. IC=0.0472, ARR=4.68% on S&P 500 over 4 years. CSI 300 primary (40.28% CSI 500 cumulative 4yr). Mutation/crossover of factor trajectories. OOS validation rigor not fully documented.
findings.reason: Interesting evolutionary approach but ARR 4.68% on S&P 500 is below our existing confirmed strategies (H217 alpha101 OOS Sharpe 1.559). Look-ahead bias documentation insufficient for staging. Note for future reference if OOS validation improved.

findings.title: AI-Driven Alpha Decay: Algorithmic Homogenization, Reflexive Signal Erosion, and the Paradox of Intelligent Markets
findings.summary: Derives h(φ) = ln2/[θ+δ(φ)]. At φ≈0.7 (current AI adoption), implies 18-month half-life vs 5-7 years pre-AI. 42% portfolio convergence increase 2013-2024 from 99.5M 13F holdings. Monoculture equilibrium: net alpha=0 when all funds use identical signals.
findings.reason: Theoretical model explaining WHY signal half-life is 18 months (not just empirical observation). Extends arXiv:2512.11913 (proposal #4) with formal derivation. Directly relevant to our H279-H281 pipeline — confirmed LLM-augmented strategies have ~18-month expected shelf life. STAGED as wiki update #5.

findings.title: FinPos: A Position-Aware Trading Agent System for Real Financial Markets
findings.summary: Dual-agent architecture (directional reasoning + risk-aware position adjustment). Multi-timescale rewards. 'Surpasses state-of-the-art trading agents in position-aware trading task.' Addresses LLM agent gap: treating each trade as isolated vs continuous position management.
findings.reason: Novel position-awareness concept relevant to H274 multi-agent PEAD upgrade (already staged). The dual-agent architecture could inform how our PEAD agent manages existing positions vs new entries. Note for H274 design document — not staging separately.

findings.title: hftbacktest
findings.summary: HFT backtesting in Rust. Order book replay, latency simulation.
findings.reason: Not relevant for monthly-rebalanced strategies. Note for future if we expand to intraday.

findings.title: gs-quant (Goldman Sachs)
findings.summary: GS Python quant toolkit: derivatives pricing, risk analytics, time series.
findings.reason: High-quality institutional toolkit. Most relevant for options pricing and derivatives. Could supplement existing vollib/QuantLib usage. Note in tools wiki.

summary: 5 high-relevance proposals staged across two sessions. Session 1 theme: LLM augmentation of existing alpha signals (H279 momentum filter, H280 multi-agent equity, H281 macro-LLM ETF tilt) + hyperbolic alpha decay (arXiv:2512.11913). Session 2 additions: AI-driven alpha decay theory (arXiv:2605.23905 — h(φ) formula, monoculture equilibrium, 18-month half-life explanation); superforecasting wiki page (Ten Commandments, domain bias table, LLM calibration layer, H185 gates). Phase 1 wiki expansion (both sessions): execution-quality.md + superforecasting-methods.md + ai-model-benchmarks.md indexed. Key new data: portfolio convergence +42% 2013-2024 from 99.5M 13F holdings; LLM strategies face ~18-month shelf life before monoculture equilibrium; political market prices on Kalshi systematically 5-8pp too close to 50% (arXiv:2602.19520).
